newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME aluminium seen a tad firm, copper flat - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium seen a tad firm, copper flat - trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium prices are seen firming slightly later on Friday while copper is likely to remain flat with the metal in the grip of a summer holiday swoon, traders said.
"Aluminium looks quite firm," a dealer said.
Three-month aluminium has good support at US$1,680/85 a tonne and will probably "try to get higher. Resistance is at $1,730 (a tonne)," another dealer said.
But Vinod Kumar, director of Singapore metal firm Donald Mcarthy, said aluminium "is overdone" and appears due for a correction.
Brokers Rudolf Wolff said in their daily review that "we expect further consolidation" in aluminium and that a correction will continue before the white metal will resume its uptrend.
Three-month aluminium was seen by one metal house at 0230 GMT at $1,697/701 a tonne against the late indication on the LME of $1,699/701 a tonne.
"For aluminium, the play will be on the cash-threes spread. There will be companies who will be selling forward. With the backwardation, there's no reason to keep the material," one trader said.
The backwardation moved out on the LME on Thursday, to $20 at one stage, after having been level earlier this week.
LME copper prices, however, are seen remaining weak.
"Copper was stagnant. It should remain stagnant," Kumar said.
"Nobody wants to do anything on copper. I don't see the Chinese in the market," another dealer said.
Three-month copper was seen by a trading firm at $2,266/71 a tonne at 0230 GMT against the kerb close on the LME of $2,271.

"The close on the lows and a potential bearish flag developing does not bode well as we look for further weaknesses to test this week's low at $2,256 and then $2,226 on a confirmed break," Rudolf Wolff said.
Zinc prices are seen firm and September tightness will probably keep them strong, dealers said.
"It should hold steady," a trader said.
Rudolf Wolff placed initial resistance at around $1,530 and then $1,560 a tonne. Three-month zinc was seen by the trade at 0230 GMT at $1,519/24 a tonne.
"The fundamentals continue to support this market's strength, with stocks in decline and the widening of the backwardation within the spread, reflecting the nearby market tightness," it said.
